highlights.description: A billing runtime that reads a product's pricing and packaging from a pricing spec: it computes the products and prices a provider should hold, starts checkout and the customer portal, and turns a paid subscription into an entitlement through ports the host supplies
Fails at startup when billing is half configured, and runs every account on the spec's default plan when no provider is configured
A Stripe adapter for customers, plan and one-time checkout, the customer portal, Connect Express sellers with destination-charge sales, catalog sync with a dry run, and webhook verification

A lifecycle that decides entitlement from the provider's current state when `Lifecycle.Provider` is set, so replays and the order webhooks arrive in do not matter, serializes concurrent handling per account when `Lifecycle.Locker` is set, and applies refunds, seller account changes and disputes through sinks

added.description: `Billing` port and `Disabled` free mode: with no provider every account is on the spec's default plan and anything that needs a provider reports it is not configured
`CheckStartup` requires a valid spec, a webhook secret (two with a marketplace) and something to sell when a provider key is set, and names what is missing without ever printing a secret
`ProviderPlanFor` computes the products and prices a provider should hold, with stable lookup keys and a `payforge_app` tag so several products can share one account
Product checkout, customers, errors and the subscription grant rule: `active`, `trialing` and `past_due` grant, and a price the spec does not have never grants
`stripe` adapter with customers keyed to the host's subject, plan and one-time checkout, and customer portal sessions; idempotency keys cover every parameter Stripe compares
Catalog sync to a Stripe account by lookup key, with a dry run; it never deletes and a changed amount creates a new price and moves the key to it
Webhook verification against several signing secrets, reduced to a normalized event; `Webhook.Mode` is required and events of the other mode are ignored
Store and entitlement-sink ports with in-memory implementations

`Lifecycle.Handle` turns subscription events into entitlements from the provider's current state, idempotent by event, skipping connected-account events and keeping events for unknown customers retryable
Connect Express accounts, onboarding links, account state and destination-charge sales with a platform fee; a sale refuses a seller that cannot take charges or that this app did not create
Refunds of payforge sales and seller account changes applied through optional sale and seller sinks

Checkout, portal and onboarding URLs must be https (or http for localhost) and are limited to `AllowedURLHosts`; `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1` are always accepted, even when the list does not name them
Prices without a lookup key grant a plan only when listed in `Lifecycle.LegacyPrices`; metadata never names a plan

Disputes and failed delayed payments become events, and disputes reach an optional `Lifecycle.Disputes` sink; the lifecycle ignores a failed delayed payment (`EventCheckoutFailed`), which the host handles itself
Optional `Locker` port serializes the lifecycle and plan checkout per account, with `MemoryLocker` for a single process; a new plan checkout expires the subject's other open ones
Examples of a catalog sync, a pricing page, a webhook endpoint and limit checks, each run by a test without a Stripe account

documentation.description: Specifications: product and technical requirements, plan and roadmap
A user guide covering the catalog, checkout and the portal, webhooks, the lifecycle, marketplaces and known limitations, built as an MkDocs site

tests.description: Tests for startup checks, free mode, lookup keys and the provider plan, with golden files
The Stripe adapter, sync, webhooks and Connect tested against a fake Stripe API that keeps state and enforces idempotency keys
`payforgetest` conformance suites for stores and sinks, and lifecycle tests for replays, late events, unknown prices and failures
An opt-in live test against Stripe's test mode that runs only with a test-mode key
